source_text: Can you get Codex to do a deep dive on how the 20k declarations you mentioned are used?

fragments.text: Can you get Codex to do a deep dive on how the 20k declarations you mentioned are used?

reply_text:
㊢ (your request) I've sent the deep dive to codex-5. It wrote the lemma checkers for this model, so it knows the files. It will work read-only and write its answer to `census/ENVINIT-USE.md` in `lean-wiring`. The job is `invoke-1790806596948-29378-f184bdc8`, parked as `park-dcf3f9ea…` with a one-hour deadline. The packet is `/tmp/pyreg/packet-envinit-dive.md`.

㊫ (what it will answer)
1. In native Lean, what runs each family and when: at module import, or only when the elaborator uses it. It cites the C and C++ sources.
2. Whether the parser registrations generated by the `@[builtin_*_parser]` attributes ended up in the "envinit" set. If they did, the split between the root sets is wrong for them, because parsing needs them.
3. A classification of the 1,948 roots, and through them the 20k declarations, into four groups:
   - needed to parse;
   - needed to elaborate Init, Std and Lean at startup;
   - needed only when a tactic, simp, grind or an option is used;
   - other.

   For each group: counts, sample names, and the rule it was read from.
4. What the port's startup does with these today, and how it stands in for Lean's module initializers.

㊟ (what I expect it to find) I expect question 2 to matter most. Builtin parsers get into Lean's parser tables only through generated initializers. If those are in the env-init set, part of the 20k is required, not optional.

㊥ (how the 20k are used) Native Lean runs all of these at startup. The C code emitted for each module calls its imports' initializers and then its own declarations' initializers (`EmitC.lean:921-943`), so everything in Init, Std and Lean is set up before the frontend begins. So startup "needs" all 20k in the sense that Lean executes them. What we don't yet know is how many of them a blank file then actually reads. That needs a trace, which I propose below. The model can't answer it on its own. Codex-5's write-up is `lean-wiring` `5bf9049`, `census/ENVINIT-USE.md`.

㊢ (codex-5's split, by what each initializer registers)

| Class | Initializer roots | Running declarations |
|---|---:|---:|
| Parser tables, categories, parser attributes | 67 | 829 |
| Elaborator setup (`Lean.Elab.*`) | 293 | 3,488 |
| Used only when a tactic, simp, grind or option is invoked | 1,518 | 15,731 |
| Other services | 70 | 125 |

The running-declaration counts sum to 20,173. The class is assigned by the namespace of the module that owns the initializer (`Lean.Parser.*` counts as parse, for instance). That rule is simple to audit, but it's a heuristic. It isn't read from how each entry is used.

㊩ (a mistake in our model) The parser definitions are correctly roots from the grammar side. But the initializers that put them into the parser tables are roots from the env-init side: parser categories, `registerBuiltinParserAttribute` (`Lean/Parser/Extension.lean:519-534`, which I checked), token tables, and so on. Even a blank-file parse depends on those. So the 67 roots / 829 declarations in the parse class belong in the startup set, and the split zai-3 made is wrong for them.

㊢ (what the port does) The port doesn't read this census. It pulls source initializers out and runs them, and it has hand-written stand-ins for parser and option initialization (`bootstrap_parser_initialization.py`, `bootstrap_option_registration.py`). Nothing checks those stand-ins against what Lean's initializers actually do. That's the gap in the curriculum on this side.

㊬ (what I checked)
- The commit is on the fork.
- The TSV's classes add up to 20,173.
- Two citations match the Lean source: `emitInitFn` and `registerBuiltinParserAttribute`.

I didn't read the classifier's code.

🈸 (next step) I propose a trace in real Lean: run the frontend on an empty file, log which registry and extension entries are looked up, and cross it with this TSV. That would turn "Lean runs 20k" into "a blank file reads N". The upper bound for what startup needs would then be the parse class plus those N. Shall I send it to codex-5?

Now the three reviewed fixes, applied in a separate worktree so kimi-1's measurement in `/tmp/mfs-real` isn't disturbed.All 16 tests pass with the fixes combined. Pushing to the fork.㊥ (branch state) `startup-linux` on the fork is now at `c30f79f`, with four fixes that were reviewed separately:
- kimi-1's alias table;
- kimi-3's compaction fix;
- zai-2's memo;
- kimi-5's cache key.

All 16 of their tests pass together. That covers only those four test files. I didn't run the rest of the suite or a cold startup. kimi-1's job ran past its last deadline and is still running, so I pushed its commit as it stood.

㊢ (kimi-1's alias fix, `2333fab`) The alias table now has all 73 builtin aliases. Each is cited to its registration call in the Lean sources (`Lean/Parser.lean`, `Extra.lean`, `Term.lean`, `Command.lean`, …). An identifier that isn't in the table now raises a named error, where before it was silently treated as an alias. The tests compare three declarations field by field against `#print` output from Lean v4.29.0. I ran them and all 8 pass.

㊟ (how "mechanical" the table is) The table is typed out in Python with a citation per entry. It isn't read from Lean when the program runs. That matches how the port records Lean facts elsewhere, but it can fall out of date if the toolchain changes.

㊩ (why kimi-1 overran) Most of its three hours went into running each test file before and after its change in `/tmp/mfs-real`. One of those background runs died without starting and had to be relaunched. It's still working on that comparison. So I applied the other fixes in a separate worktree, `/tmp/mfs-pick`, and pushed from there, which leaves the code kimi-1 is measuring untouched. `/tmp/mfs-real` catches up with a fast-forward once kimi-1 finishes.

㊩ (reproduction note is incomplete) A fresh worktree also needs `data/tmp/lean/elan/…` (a toolchain copy). Without it, tests fail with `unknown module prefix 'Init'`. The explainer's reproduction steps don't mention this, so they need a line. It's a small fix I'll add at the next docs commit.

🈳 (open question) You haven't answered the question from my last message yet: shall I send the blank-file trace in real Lean to codex-5? It would show which of the 20k initializer-reached declarations an empty file actually reads.
